correctness.rationale: A set of three distinct square-lattice points has diameter at least sqrt2 (unit-neighbor graph triangle-free); for tD<sqrt2 the occupancy is 0/1/2, with exact second factorial moment equal to g(e1)+g(e2). Near t=1/D the sole diametral pair determines the boundary of K-K: its curvature is harmonic combination κB=κpκq/(κp+κq), with second radial drop D(DκB-1)α²/2; C4 strict positive curvature, unique pair and DκB>1 give four isolated critical rotation windows. Integrating the near-contact parabolic intersection lens with κp+κq yields p2~2D^(3/2)/sqrt((κp+κq)(DκB-1))*eps² and angular density 8/(3π)(1-z²)^(3/2), squared angle Beta(1/2,5/2). The ellipse substitution reproduces 4ab²/sqrt(a²-b²); the disk exact lens instead gives (16/3)a^(3/2)eps^(3/2). Independently integrated exact elliptical covariograms (e.g. (a,b)=(2,1),(3,2) at eps=.002 ratios 1.00445 and 1.00762). Boundary cases with multiple/degenerate diameters excluded, finite integration not a proof of asymptotics.
